title: Harvesting radish microgreens
subtitle: When and how to cut, rinse, and store radish microgreen cotyledons
excerpt: Radish microgreens are ready to harvest when the cotyledons are fully open, vivid green or purple, and 5 to 8 cm tall, usually 5 to 7 days after sowing. Cut 1 cm above the medium with scissors, rinse, and use fresh or refrigerate for up to three days.
sourceNotes: UMass Extension microgreens guides (open-access). Cornell Cooperative Extension indoor growing material. Standard microgreen-growing practice synthesised from extension service material.

glossaryTerms.definition: The seed leaf — the first leaf or pair of leaves produced by a germinating seed. In most microgreen crops, the cotyledons are harvested as the edible shoot; they are larger and thicker than the true leaves that follow. Radish cotyledons are oval and smooth, ranging from pale green to deep red-purple depending on variety.

The height at which microgreens are cut above the growing medium. Cutting too low risks compost or medium contamination of the cut stems. For most microgreens, 1 cm above the surface is the standard cut height. Pea shoots and sunflower shoots are cut slightly higher (2 to 3 cm) to avoid the coarser base of the stem.

content.text: Radish microgreens are one of the fastest crops in the microgreen range: ready to cut in 5 to 7 days from sowing. The timing to harvest is simple to judge by eye: fully open cotyledons, vivid colour, 5 to 8 cm tall.

should be fully open (not still folded or cupped) and 5 to 8 cm tall measured from the medium surface. The colour should be vivid: a bright green or deep red-purple depending on variety (China Rose and Daikon produce different colour profiles). If the cotyledons are open but pale green rather than vivid, wait another 12 to 24 hours in bright light before cutting.

Do not wait too long: once the true leaves begin to appear (the smaller, lobed leaves emerging from the centre of the cotyledons), the flavour sharpens considerably and the texture coarsens. Radish microgreens are at their best just at the cotyledon stage.
Use clean, sharp scissors. Hold the shoots lightly in one hand and cut horizontally with the scissors in the other, working from one side of the tray to the other.

: cut 1 cm above the growing medium. This leaves the root system in the tray and avoids medium contamination of the cut stems. Radish microgreens do not regrow after cutting; the tray goes to compost once harvested.

Rinse cut radish microgreens under cold running water in a colander. Shake out excess water. Use fresh, or refrigerate in a sealed container lined with a piece of dry kitchen paper. The kitchen paper absorbs excess moisture and extends storage life.

Storage life: up to three days refrigerated. After three days the cotyledons begin to yellow and the peppery flavour intensifies beyond useful levels for most dishes. For the best texture and flavour, use within 24 hours of cutting.

attrs.heading: Troubleshooting
attrs.intro: Common harvest-stage problems with radish microgreens.

items.symptom: Cotyledons wilted and limp immediately after cutting
items.cause: Cut microgreens lose turgor quickly in a warm room without moisture.
items.fix: Cut directly into a bowl of cold water or into a colander over cold water to slow wilting. Use or refrigerate within 30 minutes of cutting.

items.symptom: Cut ends discolour rapidly in the refrigerator
items.cause: Excess moisture on the cut stems causes rapid browning.
items.fix: Shake or spin out excess water more thoroughly after rinsing. The kitchen paper lining in the storage container is essential, not optional.

items.symptom: True leaves have already appeared and the flavour is very sharp
items.cause: Harvested too late, past the cotyledon stage.
items.fix: Cut at the cotyledon stage: fully open, vivid colour, 5 to 8 cm tall. If true leaves are visible, the microgreen is past peak but still edible; use in smaller quantities or in cooking rather than raw.
